title: Word Search
prompt:
Given an `m x n` board of letters and a `word`, return whether the word can be traced through horizontally/vertically adjacent cells, using each cell at most once.

**Example**: board `[["A","B","C","E"],["S","F","C","S"],["A","D","E","E"]]`, word `"ABCCED"` → `true`.

DFS from every cell, matching one character at a time and marking the path to prevent reuse.
hints: Try starting the DFS at each cell.
Match `board[r][c] == word.charAt(idx)`; on success, mark the cell (e.g. set to '#'), recurse in 4 directions for idx+1, then restore.
Base case: `idx == word.length()` means the whole word matched → true.

solution.explanation: Backtracking on a grid: temporarily sinking the current cell to '#' enforces 'each cell used once' along a path, and restoring it on the way out lets other paths reuse it. The `||` short-circuits as soon as any direction completes the word.
